newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK SEEKS CAPITALBANK INSOLVENCY.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK SEEKS CAPITALBANK INSOLVENCY.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Thursday it had decided to open a bankruptcy procedure through the courts against the private Capitalbank after the BNB ascertained its insolvency.
"The BNB decided to ask the Sofia City Court to open an insolvency case against Capitalbank because its performing assets are not large enough to cover the bank's liabilities," a BNB statement said.

The amount of funds attracted by Capitalbank from individuals and companies were almost nil while its liabilities were mostly towards financial institutions and the insolvency bid could not threaten Bulgaria's banking system, the statement said.

Under the current Deposit Guarantee Law only deposits of individuals and companies in bankrupt local banks are covered by the state budget while financial institutions should wait to collect their debts in the course of those banks' liquidation.

Most of Capitalbank assets were non-performing loans worth some $20 million, which the bank could not cover by provisions or compansate them through other oparations, Capitalbank board chairman Angel Parvanov told Reuters.
Capitalbank dues to the BNB and local commercial banks totalled some $7 million. Its debt to the BNB alone totalled $3.5 million as of December 30, 1996, BNB figures showed.
The bank was licensed for domestic operations by the BNB in August 1993.

On Tuesday Capitalbank shareholders decided to raise its share capital to 12 billion levs from 1.4 billion levs through a new rights issue to in a bid to improve its capital to risk assets ratio, which is now negative, and in line with an expected rise of BNB minimum capital requirements.

Bulgaria's First Financial Company owns 47 percent of Capitalbank. Russia's Royalflesh and Bulgaria's state-owned Teraton have 25 percent each and the remaining three percent are held by another Russian firm, Rontadent.
Minimum capital requirements now are set at 1.4 billion levs for a domestic banking licence and at 2.2 billion for a full licence.
Capitalbank was the sixteenth in the row of local state and private banks whose insolvency has been sought by the BNB since May last year.

Only one of them, Madan-based Crystalbank has been declared insolvent by the court so far. Court rulings against three other banks are expected at end-March and the beginning of April. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
